title: Loongson 2K1000 real-board Git validation
current_state: Work continues on branch feature/portable-net-vf2-dwmac from commit c6b5f5f1 (feat: complete portable networking and VF2 Git validation).
RV64 and LA64 QEMU boot with the competition Alpine root filesystems; VF2 has completed real-board boot, networking, DNS, TLS, and public GitHub clone validation.
The Loongson 2K1000 Nebula board is powered and its onboard USB_DEBUG serial console has reached the U-Boot => prompt through /dev/ttyUSB0 at 115200 baud.
The available LA root filesystem is local-images/alpine-linux-loongarch64-ext4fs.img: a raw bare ext4 full Alpine root filesystem with LoongArch64 userspace and Git, not a partitioned disk image.
The repository currently exposes la64-qemu only; there is no la64-2k1000 target. Existing LA QEMU success is not evidence of 2K1000 board support.
The current LA linker uses physical load base 0x00200000, while xtask packages txv2-la.uimage for 0x90000000. The existing LA uImage must not be treated as a verified 2K1000 boot artifact.

The 2K1000 platform still needs board-specific UART/boot facts, ICU interrupt routing, AHCI storage, and ls,ls-gmac / snps,dwmac-3.70a network support before the Alpine root filesystem and Git can be validated on hardware.
The required end state is a real 2K1000 boot into the Alpine root filesystem followed by git help, local init/add/commit/log, HTTPS clone, commit, push, manual remote README edit, and pull.
Do not write or reorganize the LA knowledge handbook while bringing the board up. Complete the hardware chain first; documentation is a separate user-directed task afterward.

caveats: Never print, log, document, stage, or commit the PAT stored in local-images/git/launch-shell.sh. The local-images directory is ignored and the helper is not tracked.
Do not modify the competition LA rootfs mother image during experiments; use a copy or a disposable overlay when the transport permits it.
QEMU 10.0.2.2/10.0.2.3 networking values are QEMU user-network endpoints and must not be copied to the physical 2K1000 network configuration.
U-Boot and txKernel may program different IP and MAC values while taking turns controlling the same physical Ethernet hardware; U-Boot network state does not automatically carry into txKernel.
Keep commands short: avoid unnecessary shell variables, if branches, printf scaffolding, generated helper scripts, and destructive cleanup commands.
For every hardware step, identify the execution context, show the shortest command, show only the key success output, and state what failure means.
Do not describe intermediate repair history in user-facing knowledge documents. Record the final working chain and durable constraints only.
